Subject: Sealed Vault — architecture options (draft)

Garth / team,

Attached: sealed-vault-arch-v1.pdf and rotation-matrix.xlsx. Summary of the three recommended options (short):

1) Customer-KMS (KMIP/TCP in customer VPC) — Keys never traverse Redwood. Requirements: KMIP-compatible HSM, tunnel/peered network with port 5696 (or KMIP over TLS) and mutual auth. Pros: strongest custody. Cons: customer must ensure high-availability, backup, and key policy enforcement.

2) Envelope encryption with BYOK (customer supplies root key, Redwood holds wrapped keys) — Redwood stores only wrapped DEKs; customer rotates root BYOK via import/unwrap API. Requirements: secure import endpoint (mTLS), HSM-protected wrapping in customer environment preferred. Pros: lower ops burden for customer, Redwood can provide HA serving. Cons: customer must manage root key lifecycle.

3) Redwood-managed HSM inside customer VPC (dedicated module) — Redwood provisions an HSM appliance in-customer-network with separate operator domains. Pros: easier to operate; can offer attestation and automated rotation. Cons: contractual access controls and network isolation checklist required.

Rotation & operational notes (high-level):
- Recommended rotation cadence: root BYOK 12–24 months; DEKs 90–180 days depending on workload classification.
- Emergency unseal: prefer M-of-N operator model (2-of-3 or 3-of-5 depending on scale). We can support a hardware-backed quorum or a distributed key share solution.
- Audit & attestation: Redwood can emit signed key-operation events to your SIEM (syslog/HTTPS) and provide HSM attestation statements on key imports/rotations.

Attached doc includes network diagrams, port lists, and an initial rotation-matrix with suggested maintenance windows (UTC and local).

Happy to walk through any diagram bits on the call — sending an invite now for 4/16 10:00am PT.

Subject: Re: Sealed Vault — attestation & rotation controls (checklist)

Garth / team,

Adding a few compliance-focused constraints to the draft architecture (see attestation-checklist.md):
- Key provenance: require HSM attestation for any imported root keys (include cert chain and PCR values where applicable).
- Rotation policy: rotations must be tied to versioned key identifiers; old material must be zeroized and evidence stored.
- Access separation: operator accounts must be distinct from admin accounts and have time-bound elevation. Recommend automated rotation with manual approval window for root BYOK.
- Audit retention: store signed key-op events for minimum 7 years (can be configurable for enterprise).
- Incident playbook: include a documented emergency rewrap flow and pre-approved maintenance windows for key migration.

I'll attach the checklist to this thread. If Polaris requires FedRAMP-like artifacts we can surface HSM vendor FIPS attestation and our integration notes in a redacted pack.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
